My approach to Artificial Intelligence is deeply rooted in my background in applied mathematics. Rather than treating neural networks as black boxes, I focus on the underlying calculus, linear algebra, and optimization theory that drive them. 

My projects range from building the mathematical foundations of deep learning algorithms from scratch to applying advanced time-series models to complex physical systems.

### [ML Engine From Scratch](ml-engine.qmd)
**Language:** `Python`, `NumPy` | **Domain:** `Deep Learning Architecture`

To fully master the mathematics of automatic differentiation and backpropagation, I engineered a complete Deep Learning framework from scratch using only NumPy. 

It features an object-oriented API (similar to PyTorch), custom layers, stable cross-entropy loss functions, and a fully functional Adam optimizer. The project includes interactive Jupyter Notebooks proving the engine's capability on both non-linear classification and multi-output continuous regression.

[Explore the Framework &rarr;](ml-engine.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [OptiTherm: Digital Twin](optitherm.qmd)
**Language:** `PyTorch` | **Domain:** `Time-Series, Model Predictive Control`

A data-driven approach to modeling building thermal dynamics.

Instead of relying solely on rigid physical equations, this project uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to learn the thermal inertia and behavior of buildings directly from sensor data. The AI model is then integrated into a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework to optimize HVAC commands for maximum energy efficiency and comfort.

[View the OptiTherm Project &rarr;](optitherm.qmd)
:::
